title: KV cohorting, tail-adaptive version pinning, and onboarding playbook for long-context models
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable onboarding and release playbook that groups incoming model/sequence workloads into 'cohorts' based on long-context sequence characteristics and applies tail-adaptive version pinning and KV cache heuristics to optimize latency and stability without increasing cost risk.

Problem statement: We see per-model long-context behavior that materially affects KV cache hit rates and tail latency. Right now onboarding is manual and brittle: one-off pins or blanket retention rules cause either latency regressions for long-tail sequences or unnecessary cache pressure and cost. We need a procedure that: (1) clusters sequence distributions into cohorts, (2) derives conservative KV retention and prefetch heuristics per cohort, (3) selects a version pin strategy that minimizes fallbacks for each cohort, and (4) publishes a performance profile and rollout plan for runtime consumption.

Success criteria:
- Automated cohorting routine that groups sequences into <=6 cohorts per model with explainable characteristics (median length, tail 95/99 quantiles, repetition patterns).
- For 90% of sampled traffic, cohort-level pin choices reduce fallback events by >=40% versus current default.
- No increase in median per-token cost above 5% for the model in production during staged rollout.
- Playbook documented with step-by-step canary, metrics to watch, and rollback triggers.

Deliverables:
1) Cohorting service prototype: batch job that ingests recent request traces, extracts sequence features, runs clustering, and emits cohort signatures. Output: cohort id, representative quantiles, hot-token indicators, canonical pin recommendation. (Confluence: /drive/redwood/kv-cohorting-proto)
2) Pinning rules engine: a ruleset that maps cohort signatures to a pin decision (pin this model version, pin variant, or unpinned with fallback thresholds). Includes TTL/expiry semantics and safety net to auto-fallback to stable version on repeated errors.
3) KV heuristics per cohort: retention window suggestions, prefetch candidates, and whether to enable proactive warmup.
4) Telemetry dashboard and SLOs: cohort-level metrics (cache hit rate, fallback count, p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token cost).
5) Onboarding playbook doc: steps, PR checklist, canary thresholds, stakeholders, and links to implementation repos and runbooks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Code reviewed and merged for cohorting job and pin engine (PRs linked in comments).
- End-to-end test using synthetic long-tail traces demonstrating >40% fallback reduction and stable cost.
- Console dashboard tile implemented showing cohort breakdown and per-cohort KPIs.
- Playbook approved by Product and Reliability leads.

Risks and mitigations:
- Mis-clustering: add human-in-the-loop review for first 3 releases and conservative cohort merge rules.
- Over-pinning increases cache pressure: build simulated cache model to evaluate cost tradeoffs before rollout.
- Wrong pin leading to quality regression: pin engine must include automatic quality checks in rollout and an immediate rollback path.

Implementation notes and constraints:
- Use existing trace schema (request.trace_v2) and KV telemetry as inputs.
- Cohorting job should be idempotent and run daily; keep 14-day retention to observe drift.
- Pin decisions persisted to model-metadata store and consumable by serving runtime via existing version-gating API.

Related work: ENG-34127 (kv warmup pin expiry), ENG-62789 (seq-distribution-driven kv generator).

Open questions:
- Should cohorting include prompt structure features (function calls, system tokens) or only sequence length and repetitiveness? Propose: include a lightweight prompt-type tag to allow coarse separation.
- How aggressive should automatic expiry be for cohort pins? Default proposal: 7 days auto-expiry with renewal if stability observed.

Playbook excerpt (staged rollout):
1) Run cohorting job on last 7 days and review cohort signatures.
2) Pick 1-2 cohorts covering 30% traffic for initial canary.
3) Apply pin policy in canary namespace with pin TTL 72h and monitor fallback + latency every 15m.
4) If fallback drops >=40% and p95 latency improves or stays within 5%, widen to 60% traffic.
5) If cost delta >5% or quality signals degrade, rollback and open incident.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/kv-cohorting-proto (draft)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2145 (cohort job)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/889 (pin engine)
- Dash mock: https://app.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-cohorts

Owners: Marco Reyes (eng runtime) leads implementation; Aisha Chen (reliability) owns playbook and canary thresholds.
